Drawing & inspection checklist

Industrial and electronic enclosures with deep cavities and sealing interfaces.

Batch process control is noted in the catalog. Agree flatness and dimensional inspection criteria.

Drawing details

Locate mounting points and seal faces, and mark thin sections, masked fits and cosmetic exterior faces.

Inspection checks

Agree flatness, mounting-pattern and finish checks; an enclosure example does not imply a tested ingress-protection rating.

Requesting a quote

Provide alloy, temper, lid or gasket interfaces, finish requirements and any requested environmental testing.

Lid, gasket and mounting fit

Provide the mating lid or gasket interface and identify the mounting datums. Specify the faces that control closure and any fitted bores or threads. If environmental sealing is an objective, supply the target test and acceptance criteria; housing geometry alone cannot establish an ingress-protection rating.

Finish checks and batch reports

Mark cosmetic exterior surfaces and masked interfaces, with dimensions to check after finishing. State first-article and later-batch reporting needs alongside quantities per revision. Sample requests and sampling plans remain proposals until the inspection requirements are agreed.

Checks at each
production stage
01
Drawing and specifications

Before quoting, we review the drawing, critical dimensions, mating surfaces, material and finish to agree the inspection plan.

02
Sample inspection

Review the sample inspection results with us and resolve drawing changes before approving production.

03
Checks during production

We inspect the first article and check agreed features during manufacturing against your order requirements.

04
Final inspection and shipment

Final QC takes place before shipment, using the acceptance criteria and records agreed for your order.

See the complete manufacturing process
LZZ coordinate measuring machine. Ask us to supply current calibration records for your supplier review.

for your order

Dimensional
measurement
Coordinate measuring machine
Positions and geometric features, checked against drawing datums.
Height gauges
Heights and dimensional checks using the agreed setup.
Optical projectors
Profiles and features suited to optical measurement.

Mark any critical tolerances on your drawing. We assess them against the material and part geometry, then confirm the setup and measurement method. For selected features, ±0.01 mm may be a useful engineering reference after review, but it is not a general tolerance or guarantee. Ask us to confirm the instrument range and supply current calibration evidence. We also need to confirm which measurement records can be provided for your order.

See machining and inspection equipment
AI-generated illustration. Not an LZZ equipment photograph or measurement record.
Match the check
to the feature

Start with the drawing feature and its acceptance limits, then agree the instrument, setup and record needed for the order.

Dimensions & fit
Identify mating diameters, lengths and thread requirements. Discuss suitable dimensional tools and gauges for those features.
Heights, profiles & geometry
Define the datum system and the relationships between features. Confirm the setup and whether height, optical or coordinate measurement is appropriate.
Surface & material checks
If roughness, coating thickness or hardness matters, state the method and acceptance criteria. Confirm which checks and records can be supplied.
Discuss inspection requirements →
Inspection records
for your order
Dimensional results

Identify critical features and the first-article or dimensional report format you need. Specify the datums and whether dimensions apply before or after finishing.

Material & treatment records
Surface & batch acceptance
Make acceptance clear before machining

Use this blank example to discuss the report you need. We agree the features to measure and sampling plan from your approved drawing, together with the measurement method.

Blank example only. It contains no customer data, measured results or approval.

Ask LZZ to confirm which records can be supplied for your order before machining. No customer report or measurement result is published on this site.

Prepare your drawing and inspection checklist
ISO 9001-certified
quality management

LZZ is ISO 9001 certified. The enterprise-recognition documents shown on our About page are separate awards, not the ISO certificate or a product approval.

View company documents
Company recognition documents
ISO 9001 certification & order checks
Feature-specific tolerance review
Inspection and material documents
First-article inspection

We provide first-article inspection against the agreed drawing features. Define the report format, sampling and any customer approval hold point before batch production.

Dimensional records

We record the specified features, drawing limits, measurement method and results, identified by part number, drawing revision and part or batch reference.

Material documents

We supply the material documents specified in the order. Agree the grade, condition and required traceability when quoting so procurement retains the necessary records.

Finishing documents

We arrange the treatment documentation required by the order, linked to the specified process and part or batch. State any special acceptance test or document requirement before production.

Your quotation will list the included documents and any extra cost. The services above are not reports from a completed order. If you are qualifying LZZ as a supplier, request the ISO certificate and current calibration records separately.

First-article inspection

We provide first-article inspection against the agreed drawing features. Define the report format, sampling and any customer approval hold point before batch production.

Dimensional records

We record the specified features, drawing limits, measurement method and results, identified by part number, drawing revision and part or batch reference.

Material documents

We supply the material documents specified in the order. Agree the grade, condition and required traceability when quoting so procurement retains the necessary records.

Finishing documents

We arrange the treatment documentation required by the order, linked to the specified process and part or batch. State any special acceptance test or document requirement before production.

Your quotation will list the included documents and any extra cost. The services above are not reports from a completed order. If you are qualifying LZZ as a supplier, request the ISO certificate and current calibration records separately.
